title: Finite quotient by a root of the prime parameter

from.place: step 4 of its split (source: Lemma 59.73.13 (Tag 09Z5), proof of (1)); within it, 'Applying Lemma lemma-tate-japanese once more with x = p in Lambda we reduce yet again to the case of a field', proof of Algebra 032W (via lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-nagata); this node supplies the closed-fibre finiteness part of Tate used at that place; specifically the description of yS and residue-field argument of Tag 032P, steps 3--7 of the closed-fibre node

source.place: Algebra, Tag 032P (lemma-tate-japanese), proof from the description of the prime yS through finiteness of S/yS; the zero-parameter case uses the definition of N-2

statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] with fraction field $K$, and let $L/K$ be a finite field extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] in characteristic a prime $p$. Let $x\in R$ with $R/xR$ a domain and N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. Fix an integer $e\geq 0$ such that every $a\in L$ satisfies $a^{p^e}\in K$. Put $S=\operatorname{integralClosure}_R(L)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. If $y\in S$ satisfies $y^{p^e}=x$, then $S/yS$ is a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

proof.text: Apply tate_root_ideal_prime to identify Q=yS as a prime with contraction xR. This also handles the zero parameter without an N-2 transport to R.
The original finite extension L/K makes L a fraction field of S=integralClosure R L. Apply principal_prime_quotient_fraction_finite to obtain a finite extension of quotient fraction fields.

Put A=R/(Q contraction), B=S/Q. The equality of the contraction with xR transports the given IsN2 hypothesis to A. The canonical A -> B is injective and integral, and A is Noetherian. Shrink FractionRing B to the universe of A using its finite basis and apply N-2. Transport the finite integral closure back along the shrink algebra equivalence. Embed B linearly into this closure using the injective fraction map and integrality. Noetherianity makes B finite over A. Restrict scalars along the finite quotient R -> A.

proof_origin.place: Tag 032P, root ideal and residue-field argument; formalized by S3, with quotient fraction fields and universe shrinking.

theorem tate_root_closure_quotient_finite
    (R : Type u) (K L : Type v) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
    [Algebra K L] [Algebra R L] [IsScalarTower R K L]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] (x : R) (hnormal : IsIntegrallyClosed R)
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP K p] [FiniteDimensional K L]
    [IsDomain (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({x} : Set R))]
    (hquot : IsN2 (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({x} : Set R))
      (FractionRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({x} : Set R))))
    (e : ℕ) (hpow : ∀ a : L, a ^ (p ^ e) ∈ (algebraMap K L).range)
    (y : integralClosure R L)
    (hy : y ^ (p ^ e) = algebraMap R (integralClosure R L) x) :
    Module.Finite R ((integralClosure R L) ⧸ Ideal.span ({y} : Set (integralClosure R L)))
